lines.japanese: １１時過ぎ、俺たちはリラクゼーションスペースを謳った全国チェーンの漫画喫茶に入った。
lines.english: A little after eleven, we entered a branch of a nationwide manga-café chain that advertised itself as a ‘relaxation space.’

lines.japanese: 俺が行こうと思っていたところじゃなくて、そのはす向かいのビル。いつの間にか付いてくることになっていた亜衣が、そっちの店を強く勧めたからだ。
lines.english: It wasn't the place I'd meant to visit, but the building diagonally across from it. Ai, who had somehow wound up coming along, had strongly recommended this one.

lines.japanese: 「値段はこっちのがチョイ高なんだけど、綺麗だし静かだし臭くないよ」
lines.english: “This one's a little pricier, but it's clean and quiet and doesn't stink.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、臭くないって」
lines.english: “What do you mean, ‘doesn't stink’?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、あるじゃん、なんか臭い漫喫って」
lines.english: “Come on. Some manga cafés just smell.”

lines.japanese: ひどい言い草だ。心当たりないこともないけど。
lines.english: What a thing to say. Not that I didn't know what she meant.

lines.japanese: 「……狭いな」
lines.english: “...It's cramped.”

lines.japanese: 「しょーがないよ、オープン席もペアシートも埋まってたんだから」
lines.english: “Can't be helped. The open seats and the two-person booths were all taken.”

lines.japanese: 「ええーっ！　しょーがなくないよー、ひとり関係ないひとが混じってるからだよー」
lines.english: “What!? It could've been helped! There's one completely unrelated person crammed in here with us!”

lines.japanese: 俺の当初のイメージでは、横一列の開放的な並び席に鳴が座り、俺がその後ろに突っ立って画面を見守る──という感じだったんだけど。
lines.english: What I'd pictured was Naru at one of a row of open terminals, with me standing behind her to watch the screen.

lines.japanese: こんな、一名用の個室に三人も押しこまれるなんて想定外だ。
lines.english: I hadn't planned on cramming three people into a private booth built for one.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ。三人分カネ払ってんのにこの状況って、なんか、かなり理不尽じゃね？」
lines.english: “Listen. We paid for three people and *this* is what we get? Doesn't that seem seriously unreasonable?”

lines.japanese: 「しょーがないよ。漫喫って基本的にひとりで過ごすとこだもん、グループで押しかけるこっちがイレギュラーなんだよ」
lines.english: “Can't be helped. Manga cafés are basically for spending time alone. We're the weird ones, barging in as a group.”

lines.japanese: 「ええーっ！　しょーがなくないよー、ひとり関係ないひとが混じってるからだよー」
lines.english: “What!? It could've been helped! There's one completely unrelated person crammed in here with us!”

lines.japanese: ひとり掛けのソファーに座った鳴が、不服をこぼしながら右手でネズミ風の装置を動かしはじめた。
lines.english: Still airing her grievance from the one-person sofa, Naru began moving a mouse-shaped device with her right hand.

lines.japanese: 人差し指がネズミのケツを叩くたび、画面の絵や文字が入れかわっていってる。
lines.english: Every time her index finger smacked the mouse’s ass, the pictures and text on the screen changed.

lines.japanese: 「何コレ。コレがインターネットってやつなの。つか、字ィ小っちぇーなこのテレビ。おー、目ぇ悪くすんぞコレ」
lines.english: “What's this? This is that internet thing? And the writing's tiny on this TV. Whoa, this'll ruin your eyes.”

lines.japanese: 「テレビじゃないよ。なんか隼人君、おじいちゃんみたいなこと言うね」
lines.english: “It's not a TV. Hayato, you sound like somebody's grandpa.”

lines.japanese: 「ばか、知ってるっつの。そっちのアレ、アレだろ、キーボードってんだろ」
lines.english: “Idiot, I knew that. And that thing there—that's a, you know, a keyboard.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は『鷹は舞いおりた』の名刺を横に置いて、それをちらちら見ながら角ボタンだらけの板の上で十本の指を躍らせる。なんでボタンを見てないのに操作ができるんだろう。超能力者か、こいつ。
lines.english: Naru set *The Hawk Has Landed* business card beside her and, glancing back and forth at it, made all ten fingers dance across the board of square buttons. How could she work it without looking at the buttons? Was she psychic?

lines.japanese: エスパー鳴は、折れ矢印の書かれたでっかいボタンを最後にばちんと押して振りむいた。
lines.english: Naru the Psychic finished by smacking the huge key with the bent arrow, then turned around.

lines.japanese: 「はいー、きのう言ったＢＢＳに入りましたよー。さー隼人さん、どうぞー」
lines.english: “There—we’re on the BBS I mentioned yesterday. All yours, Hayato, sir.”
“Ah. Right...”

lines.japanese: 鳴が席を立つ。俺はよく分からない流れに呑まれて、なんとなくソファーに滑りこんだ。
lines.english: Naru stood. Carried along by a turn of events I didn't understand, I found myself sliding onto the sofa.

lines.japanese: 「あー、で……どうすんのコレ」
lines.english: “Uh, so... what do I do with this?”

lines.japanese: 俺は人差し指を下唇に当て、穢れを知らぬ少年のような瞳でネズミ装置を見下ろした。
lines.english: I touched one finger to my lower lip and gazed down at the mouse device with the unsullied eyes of an innocent boy.

lines.japanese: 「はあ、えーと、いちばん上が新しい記事なので、適当に下へ送っていただければ」
lines.english: “Well, um, the newest post is at the top, so just scroll down however you like...”

lines.japanese: 「違うよ鳴ちゃん、隼人君きっとマウス触ったことないんだよ」
lines.english: “No, Naru. Hayato's probably never touched a mouse before.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　えっ？　そうなんですか？」
lines.english: “What? What? Is that true?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ。よく分かんねーけど、マウスってこのネズミのこと」
lines.english: “Beats me. Is the ‘mouse’ this rat here?”

lines.japanese: 俺はマウスとやらの尻尾を掴んでぷらぷら持ちあげた。
lines.english: I caught the so-called mouse by its tail and dangled it in the air.

lines.japanese: 「あらま！」
lines.english: “Well, I'll be!”

lines.japanese: 鳴はカルチャーショックを絵にしたようなツラで驚いた。俺はちょっぴり傷付いた。
lines.english: Naru stared at me like culture shock made flesh. It hurt a little.

lines.japanese: 「もー、鳴ちゃん冷たいよねー。思いやりがないよねー。相手の立場でものごと考えられないよねー」
lines.english: “Honestly, Naru, you're so cold. No consideration at all. You can't put yourself in the other person's shoes.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ！　えーっ、違うよ事故だよー、現代人の常識を逆手に取った情報化社会の落とし穴だよー」
lines.english: “What!? No, that was an accident! An information-age trap that turns modern common sense against you!”

lines.japanese: 「ね隼人君、画面のそこにほら、白い矢印あるでしょ。それがカーソルって言うんだけど──」
lines.english: “Look, Hayato. See the white arrow on the screen? That's called the cursor—”

lines.japanese: 「え、どれ」
lines.english: “Wait, where?”

lines.japanese: 「亜衣ちゃんどいてよー、私が教えるからー」
lines.english: “Ai, move! I'll teach him!”

lines.japanese: 「何いまさら！　鳴ちゃん、自分から席離れたんじゃん。一度でも子の元を離れた親に、戻ってくる資格なんてないですよ、ぺっぺっ！」
lines.english: “Too late! You were the one who left your seat. A mother who leaves her child even once has no right to come back. Ptooey, ptooey!”

lines.japanese: 「えー、亜衣ちゃんなんか、ただの通りすがりのおばさんのくせにー！　もぉー、この押し掛け女房！　へやっ、へやっ！」
lines.english: “What!? You're just some random old lady off the street! You barged in here playing wife! Hyah! Hyah!”

lines.japanese: 「きぃーっ！　産みの親より育ての親！　産みの親より育ての親！」
lines.english: “Why, you—! The real mother is the one who raises you! The real mother is the one who raises you!”

lines.japanese: 「てっ、あてっ……ばか、やめろおまえら、狭いんだから暴れんなよ」
lines.english: “Ow—ow! Idiots, quit it! It's cramped in here. Don't start fighting.”

lines.japanese: 小娘どもが俺の頭越しに、きゃいきゃいとこぶしの応酬を始めた（そしてそれは、ほとんどが流れ弾となって俺の脳天に着弾した）。
lines.english: The little brats began squealing and trading punches over my head. Almost every stray shot landed square on my skull.

lines.japanese: 「痛てっ、痛てっ……てめっ、やめっ……や、やめろてめえ、痛えっつんだよサル共──」
lines.english: “Ow, ow... You little—stop... I said stop, you goddamn monkeys, that hurts—”

lines.japanese: 「あの、お客様……」
lines.english: “Excuse me...”

lines.japanese: 「すみませんが店内ではお静かに願えますでしょうか」
lines.english: “I'm sorry, but could you please keep your voices down?”

lines.japanese: 「ご、ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “S-sorry.”

lines.japanese: 簡易扉の向こうから届いた冷ややかな叱責に、なぜだか非のない俺が謝ってしまった。
lines.english: Though I was the only innocent party, for some reason I was the one who apologized when the chilly rebuke came through the flimsy door.

lines.japanese: いきなり二児の父親になった気分だ。
lines.english: I felt as though I'd suddenly become a father of two.

lines.japanese: 「くっそ、このアホザル共が……」
lines.english: “Goddammit, you stupid little monkeys...”

lines.japanese: 「おー、よう、どっちでもいいから早く教えろよ。なに、カーソル？　どれだカーソルって」
lines.english: “Hey. Either one of you—hurry up and teach me. What was it, the cursor? Which thing's the cursor?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ほら、そこだよ隼人君」
lines.english: “Right there, Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 亜衣が俺の後ろから肩越しに指を伸ばす。俺の後頭部にやつの体重がのしかかってきた。なだらかな硬い感触。もはや慣れたというより飽きたと言う方が相応しい──
lines.english: Ai reached over my shoulder from behind. Her weight settled against the back of my head. A smooth, firm sensation. By now, ‘bored of it’ was probably more accurate than ‘used to it’—

lines.japanese: 「ああーっ！　当ててるーっ！」
lines.english: “Aaah! She's pressing her chest against you!”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　んだよ、っせえな」
lines.english: “Huh? What? Shut up.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ鳴ちゃん、静かにしないとまた店員さんに怒られるよ。隣りのお客さんにも迷惑だし」
lines.english: “She's right, Naru. Keep your voice down or the clerk will scold us again. You'll bother the people next door too.”

lines.japanese: いや、隣りは右も左も俺たちが取った（取らされた）空き部屋だけど。
lines.english: Except we had taken—or been made to take—the empty booths on both our right and left.

lines.japanese: 「もぉーっ！　私が教える、亜衣ちゃん邪魔ー！　姑息ー！　淫売ー！」
lines.english: “Oh, come on! *I'm* teaching him! Ai, move! Cheat! Whore!”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、こんな特等席ぜったい譲らないもーん。んふーん♪」
lines.english: “Hmph. No way I'm giving up a front-row seat like this. Mm-hmm-hmm♪”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい誰だクソガキ。ひとの頭の上で頬杖つくなコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey. Which brat is it? Don't rest your chin on top of my head, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「もぉー！　いいよもー、亜衣ちゃんが上なら私こっちー！」
lines.english: “Fine! If Ai gets the upper spot, I'll take this one!”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ええええっ！？」
lines.english: “What!?”

lines.japanese: 「さー、教壇に立った鳳先生がばりばり教えますよー」
lines.english: “All right, Ms. Otori is at the podium and ready to teach!”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、いや、おまえ立ってねーじゃん座ってんじゃん」
lines.english: “You're not at a podium. You're sitting down.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃねーよ、じゃなくて、嫁入り前の娘がどこ座ってんだよおまえ」
lines.english: “No, wait, that ain't the point. Where the hell do you think an unmarried girl is sitting?”

lines.japanese: 「ばりばりっ、ばりばりっ」
lines.english: “Hard at work! Hard at work!”

lines.japanese: 「つか、ばりばり教えるって、口でばりばり言うだけかよ」
lines.english: “You said you'd work hard, but all you're doing is chanting ‘hard at work.’”

lines.japanese: 「ほらほら、いいから隼人君！　そこほら、右端に長い棒があるでしょ。それがスクロールバーね」
lines.english: “Come on, Hayato! Look. There's a long bar on the right edge. That's the scroll bar.”

lines.japanese: 「隼人さん隼人さん、そんなものより、こっちにはページダウンという便利なキーがあるんですよ」
lines.english: “Hayato, Hayato, forget that. Over here, we have a convenient key called Page Down.”

lines.japanese: 「う、動くなばかっ、なんかもぞもぞするっつの！」
lines.english: “D-don't move, idiot! You're fidgeting!”

lines.japanese: 「ほらこれっ、ページダウンこれっ！　ほらほらすごいっ！　指一本でラクラク操作、見たいところに自由自在！　あとこっち、これページアップ！　ページアップこれっ！」
lines.english: “Here, this one! Page Down! Look, look, isn't it marvelous? Easy one-finger operation! Go wherever you please! And this one over here is Page Up! This is Page Up!”

lines.japanese: 俺の脚のあいだで、無駄に張りきる鳳先生の頭が揺れていた。俺は男の子のデリケートな部分がページアップしないよう、ソファーをこっそり後ろに引いた。
lines.english: Ms. Otori's needlessly enthusiastic head bobbed between my legs. To keep the delicate part of my male anatomy from paging up, I quietly edged the sofa backward.

lines.japanese: すると（あ、やべっ）後頭部が亜衣のペラい体に沈みこんだ。
lines.english: Then—ah, shit—the back of my head sank into Ai's paper-thin body.

lines.japanese: 「いやーん、隼人君だいたーん」
lines.english: “Oh my, Hayato. How bold.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うるせっ、偶然だ偶然」
lines.english: “Sh-shut up. It was an accident.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ちょぉー！　隼人さん、なにやってんですかー！」
lines.english: “What? Hey! Hayato, what are you doing?”

lines.japanese: 「ばっ、ばかおまっ、そのポジショニングで振りむくなっ」
lines.english: “I-idiot, don't turn around from that position!”

lines.japanese: 俺は鳴の頭を両腕で掴み、その場に固定した。
lines.english: I caught Naru's head in both hands and fixed it in place.

lines.japanese: 「なー！　なんでですかー、見せられないような授業内容なんですかー！」
lines.english: “Hey! Why not? Is this lesson something you can't let me see?!”

lines.japanese: 「あぁ～ん、そこはだめぇ～ん」
lines.english: “Ooh, you mustn't touch me there…”

lines.japanese: 「ええーっ、いま私の後ろで密着いけない個人指導ー！？」
lines.english: “What!? Forbidden hands-on private instruction is happening behind my back?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえっつの！　てめえらもう黙ってろ、ブッ殺すぞコノ──」
lines.english: “I told you, shut up! Both of you be quiet or I'll fucking kill you, assh—”

lines.japanese: 「お、お客様！　お客様、店内での不純異性交遊は！」
lines.english: “C-customers! Lewd relations between the sexes are prohibited inside the establishment!”

lines.japanese: 「してねえよ」
lines.english: “We’re not doing anything.”

lines.japanese: 掲示板の見方をざっと教わった俺は、騒がしい教師どもを隣りの個室へ追いやり、ひとりでじっくりとそこに並ぶ情報を閲覧していた。
lines.english: Once they'd taught me the rough basics of reading the board, I drove my noisy teachers into the booth next door and settled in to examine the information alone.

lines.japanese: そして──すぐに目が疲れてきた。あと頭も。
lines.english: And before long my eyes began to ache. My head too.

lines.japanese: もともと俺が活字とか苦手ってのは大きいけれど、それでなくとも、掲示板のやつらはヴィジュアル系気取りな言いまわしや仲間うちで流行ってるっぽい隠語を多用してて一見さんに優しくない雰囲気だ。
lines.english: I was never much of a reader, but that wasn’t the only problem. The posters wrote like members of some flamboyant rock band and peppered everything with insider slang. The place wasn’t exactly welcoming to newcomers.

lines.japanese: そもそもＲ－ウィングの母体は、ロックバードなるアマチュアバンドのファンクラブなわけだから、俺にはまったく知識も興味もない音楽ネタが話題の多くを占めている。
lines.english: R-Wing had started as the fan club of an amateur band called Rockbird, so naturally most of the discussion was music talk I neither understood nor cared about.

lines.japanese: とくに、自己破壊願望を開陳したお耽美ポエムや、ソフトめの性倒錯を綴ったセックス白書、ドラッグ嗜好を臭わせるような趣味の悪いデカダン日記は、俺の美意識からかけ離れていて反吐が出そうだった。
lines.english: Worst were the precious little poems romanticizing self-harm, the sex reports candidly confessing mild perversions, and the tasteless diaries affecting drug-addled decadence. All of it lay so far outside my own tastes that it made me want to puke.

lines.japanese: くだらねえ。
lines.english: Garbage.

lines.japanese: 鳴の言うところでは「えー、過去半年分のログが残ってますねー」とのことだったが、時間も限られてることだし、俺はここ数日分の書き込みに絞りこんで目を通した。
lines.english: According to Naru, the logs went back six months. Our time was limited, though, so I kept to the last few days' posts.

lines.japanese: そして、それは正解だったみたいだ。掲示板の雰囲気が変わってきたのは、ちょうどその辺りから──
lines.english: That seemed to have been the right choice. It was around then that the atmosphere of the board began to change—

lines.japanese: ──変革は、柳木原少年自警団を名乗る“敵”の出現によって。
lines.english: —with the appearance of an “enemy” calling itself the Yanagihara Youth Vigilantes.

lines.japanese: 当然っちゃ当然だけど、俺の知らないところでもＲ－ウィングと柳木原フレイムバーズは、大なり小なり数々のいさかいを起こしていたみたいだ。
lines.english: It made sense, but apparently R-Wing and the Yanagihara Flame Birds had been getting into clashes large and small without my knowing a thing about it.

lines.japanese: それまで自分の手首や胸に可愛い傷を刻み、破滅を謳った平和な国の音楽に酔いしれ、睡眠剤や咳止めシロップで手慰み程度のクスリ遊びに興じていた子供たちは、そうして暴力という新たな娯楽に愉悦を見出した。
lines.english: Until then, the children had carved adorable little wounds into their wrists and chests, swooned over the ruin-worshipping music of their peaceful country, and played at drugs with sleeping pills and cough syrup. Now they’d found a new pastime in violence.

lines.japanese: 何人やっただの誰々がやられただのを箇条書きで述べた文字列は、まるで大掛かりなサバイバルゲームの経過報告みたいで現実味がない。
lines.english: The strings of text listing how many they had taken out and exactly who had gone down read like progress reports from one enormous airsoft match. None of it felt real.

lines.japanese: 現実味がない──だからきっと、やつらもこんな冗談みたいな戦争ごっこを続けていられたんじゃないか。すべては憶測に過ぎないけれど。
lines.english: It didn't feel real—and perhaps that was precisely why they could keep playing at this ridiculous little war. But that was only speculation.

lines.japanese: １１月２２日。ハリュー襲撃せらるの報が投じられ、一気に書き込みの量が増える。そこには狂信的なガキ共の青臭い怒りがほとばしっていた。
lines.english: November 22. Word came that Haryu had been attacked, and the volume of posts exploded. The callow fury of fanatical children poured across the screen.

lines.japanese: １１月２３日。血走った信者たちは、聖戦の名のもと、各所でフレイムバーズの下部組織に“討ち入り”を仕掛けた。
lines.english: November 23. In the name of holy war, the bloodshot faithful launched ‘raids’ on Flame Birds affiliates all over town.

lines.japanese: その中に混じって記されていた、敵と誤認して“勇敢にして寛大なる隼”に刃物を向けた男の話に、俺は心当たりがあった。投稿者の名前は「咲夜」。
lines.english: Among those accounts was the story of a man who mistook the “valiant and magnanimous Falcon” for an enemy and drew a knife on him. I recognized the incident. The poster’s name was Sakuya.

lines.japanese: “隼は孤高。孤高なれば敵にあらず味方にあらず。志を近しくする同朋と見つけたり”
lines.english: *The Falcon stands alone. In solitude, neither foe nor friend. Yet in him have we found a comrade of kindred purpose.*

lines.japanese: 同朋じゃねえよ。誉めるな、俺を誉めるな。
lines.english: I'm not your comrade. Don't praise me. Stop praising me.

lines.japanese: さらに、その下に「特設ページへ」という文字、それからごちゃごちゃした小さな英数字が並んでいたけど、それはさっぱり意味が分からない。無視しよう。
lines.english: Underneath were the words ‘To the Special Page,’ followed by a jumble of tiny letters and numbers. I couldn't make head or tail of them. Ignore it.

lines.japanese: １１月２４日。激化する戦渦。被害と憎しみの輪が広がり、いよいよ物騒なことをほざくやつも出てきた。飛び道具を手に入れたとほのめかしているのが、おそらくあのオウム頭の大司教だろう──
lines.english: November 24. The war intensified. As the cycle of injury and hatred widened, people began spouting genuinely dangerous things. The one hinting that he’d acquired a ranged weapon was presumably that parrot-headed Archbishop—

lines.japanese: ──投稿者名は「パトリアーク・ヨーゼフ」。覚えにくい。やっぱ大司教でいい。もしくはオウム、もしくは馬鹿だ。
lines.english: —posting under the name ‘Patriarch Josef.’ Hard to remember. Archbishop would do. Or Parrot. Or Idiot.

lines.japanese: しかし気になったのが、その飛び道具の入手経路だ。そこには「社会を蝕む蛇蠍より奪取せり」とある。
lines.english: What bothered me was where the ranged weapon had come from. *Seized from the serpents and scorpions that gnaw at society,* the post said.

lines.japanese: 奪取せり──つまり、その種の売人から買ったものではないらしい。あんな物騒なおもちゃ、どこのどなたから盗んだって言うんだろう。
lines.english: *Seized*—so apparently he hadn't bought it from a dealer in that kind of thing. Just who had he stolen such a dangerous toy from?

lines.japanese: 俺はマウスから手を放し、鳴たちが置いていってくれた飲み放題の炭酸飲料で喉を潤した。
lines.english: I took my hand off the mouse and drank from one of the free-refill sodas Naru and Ai had left me.

lines.japanese: １１月２５日。ついに大司教の召集命令が下った。
lines.english: November 25. At last, the Archbishop issued the order to muster.

lines.japanese: “主の快復近し。今宵、ロックバードの再臨なるやもしれず。総員、身を濯ぎて聖地に集え”
lines.english: *Our Lord’s recovery is near. Tonight may witness the second coming of Rockbird. Let all purify themselves and gather upon the holy ground.*

lines.japanese: ２５日と言えばこの前の土曜日。そうだ、間違いない。ガード下でアホ共が衝突したあの日だ。
lines.english: The twenty-fifth was last Saturday. Right. No mistake. The day those idiots collided beneath the overpass.

lines.japanese: ここには記されていないが、もちろん俺はその後のあらましを知っている。オウムとニワトリ、親分同士の一騎打ちは前者の大敗で終わった。
lines.english: It wasn't recorded here, but of course I knew what followed. Parrot and Chicken, the two bosses, fought one on one. Parrot got demolished.

lines.japanese: 果たして翌１１月２６日。不毛な戦争ごっこに幕が閉じられている。
lines.english: And so, on November 26, the futile little war came to an end.

lines.japanese: “終戦協定、締結せり”
lines.english: *Armistice concluded.*

lines.japanese: あとは森里たちから聞いたとおりだった。大司教は重傷を負って病院へ運びこまれた。戦意と戦力を大きく失ったＲ－ウィングは柳木原フレイムバーズの軍門に降り、それを良しとしない者は潔くチームを去っている。
lines.english: The rest matched what Morisato and the others had told me. The Archbishop was badly injured and taken to a hospital. With both its strength and will to fight broken, R-Wing surrendered to the Yanagihara Flame Birds. Anyone who couldn't stomach that made a clean break and left the group.

lines.japanese: どちらにせよ、その後の掲示板には、一過性のムーブメントが過ぎたあとに残るある種の無常観が漂っていた。
lines.english: Either way, the posts that followed were steeped in the peculiar sense of transience left behind when a passing craze had run its course.

lines.japanese: たとえばペットボトルのおまけを馬鹿みたいに集めまくって、しかしふと熱が冷めたときに決まって訪れる、あの後悔とまでは呼べない気まずげな空気だ。
lines.english: That awkward feeling—not quite regret—that always came after you’d collected giveaway trinkets from plastic drink bottles like an idiot, then suddenly lost all interest.

lines.japanese: 掲示板は急速に活気を失い、以前のような訳知り顔の音楽評論だけが埋み火のようにくすぶっていた。
lines.english: The board rapidly went quiet. Only the same smug music criticism as before smoldered on like embers under ash.

lines.japanese: １１月２７日。口数の少ないたまり場に、反撃ののろしをあげよと檄が飛んだ。投稿者はパトリアーク・ヨーゼフ──白いパイプベッドを抜けだした手負いのオウムだ。
lines.english: November 27. Into that sullen silence came a fiery summons to raise the beacon of counterattack. The poster was Patriarch Josef—the wounded Parrot, escaped from his white hospital bed.

lines.japanese: “我らが主の聖痕にかけて、赦されざる咎に裁きを！　紅き涙をもって朱き血を漱がん！”
lines.english: *By the stigmata of our Lord, judgment upon the unforgivable transgression! With crimson tears shall scarlet blood be cleansed!*

lines.japanese: しかしそれは、消えかかった火にわざわざ湿った焚き木を放りこんだようなものだった。
lines.english: But it was like going out of his way to throw damp firewood on a dying flame.

lines.japanese: Ｒ－ウィングの残党にとってみればフレイムバーズとの戦争ごっこはすでに終わった遊びだし、ましてや敗軍の将が兵を語るなど不快以外のなにものでもない。
lines.english: To R-Wing’s remnants, the war with the Flame Birds was a game already over. Having their defeated commander lecture them about war was more than they could stomach.

lines.japanese: 誰かが匿名でぽつりと言った。もう大司教は放置しろ。
lines.english: One anonymous poster quietly said: *Leave the Archbishop alone.*

lines.japanese: １１月２８日。掲示板上の何人かが“やくざ風の男たちから大司教の所在を尋ねられた”という旨を報告している。
lines.english: November 28. Several people on the board reported that ‘men who looked like mobsters had asked where the Archbishop was.’

lines.japanese: “社会を蝕む蛇蠍より奪取せり”
lines.english: *Seized from the serpents and scorpions that gnaw at society.*

lines.japanese: なるほど……そういうことか……。
lines.english: I see... So that was it...

lines.japanese: 俺は把握した。あの馬鹿は絶望的なまでに馬鹿だ。やつは暴力団組員から銃を盗んだんだ。
lines.english: I understood. That idiot was stupid beyond hope. He'd stolen the gun from a mobster.

lines.japanese: 病院を抜けだしたのは、医者や警察や少年自警団が恐かったからじゃない。もっと話の通じない種族の、非人道的なおしおきを逃れるためだ。
lines.english: He hadn't fled the hospital because he feared the doctors, the police, or the youth vigilantes. He was escaping inhuman punishment at the hands of a species even less open to reason.

lines.japanese: そして１１月２９日、つまり今日。投稿時刻は未明、いまから２０時間ほど前。もはやこの場においては厄介者でしかないヨーゼフ大司教からの書き込みがあった。
lines.english: Then came November 29—today. The post was from before dawn, roughly twenty hours ago. Archbishop Josef, by now nothing but a nuisance to everyone there, had written again.

lines.japanese: やつは仲間に見放された悲痛と絶望を、恨みがましい抒情詩と呪詛の祈りに託して愁訴した。
lines.english: He poured the anguish and despair of abandonment into resentful lyric verse and prayers of malediction.

lines.japanese: いわく“この命、長くはないだろう。だが見ているがいい、かつて朋輩と呼んだ者たちよ。私は必ずや赦されざる罪に裁きをくだす”
lines.english: He declared: *My life cannot last much longer. But watch, you whom I once called comrades. I shall without fail bring judgment upon the unforgivable transgression.*

lines.japanese: さらにいわく“我、憎き咎人を死出の旅路に同道させん”
lines.english: And further: *I shall take the hateful sinner with me on the road to death.*

lines.japanese: つまり「オレは死ぬからアイツも殺す」だ。滅多なことを言うやつ、そう思ったのは俺だけじゃない。元仲間たちでさえ、文字に滲みでるほどドン引いていた。
lines.english: In other words: ‘I'm dying, so I'm taking him with me.’ I wasn't alone in thinking those were dangerous words. Even his former comrades were recoiling so hard you could see it in the text.

lines.japanese: しかし……あの狂った男が言う「殺す」は、どっかの善良な男の子が口にする「ブッ殺す」とは意味が違う。やつは命ある人間に向けて引き金を引ける人種だった。
lines.english: But... when that lunatic wrote *kill,* it meant something different from a certain decent young man's ‘I'll fucking kill you.’ He was the kind of human being who could pull a trigger on another living person.

lines.japanese: このことを──つまり、死すら覚悟した狂人に命が狙われていることを、あの手負いのニワトリは知っているのだろうか。
lines.english: Did that wounded Chicken know? Know that a madman ready even for death was after his life?

lines.japanese: 俺はふたたびグラスに口を付けた。
lines.english: I raised the glass to my lips again.

lines.japanese: ……まあ……問題ない……か。
lines.english: ...Well... it should be fine... probably.

lines.japanese: 大司教のトカレフは暗き河の底。すでに味方もいない。鳳翔なら鎧袖一触で追いはらえる相手だ。
lines.english: The Archbishop's Tokarev lay at the bottom of a dark river, and he had no allies left. Kakeru Otori could swat him aside with one brush of his armored sleeve.

lines.japanese: それになによりあのオウム頭は、一刻も早く柳木原から逐電しなければならない身だ。そう何度も復讐の機会はないだろう。
lines.english: More than anything, Parrot Head had to get out of Yanagihara as fast as he could. He couldn’t have many chances left for revenge.

lines.japanese: それでも……それでも俺は、あのニワトリに念のため忠告ぐらいはしておいてやろう。俺は一度やつに命を救われている。
lines.english: Even so... even so, I ought to warn Chicken, if only as a precaution. He'd saved my life once.

lines.japanese: それに……それに、あいつにだって、何かあれば悲しむ身内ぐらいいる。
lines.english: And... and even he had family who would grieve if something happened to him.

lines.japanese: しかし、そうなると、いままで考えたこともなかった問題が持ちあがる。
lines.english: But that raised a problem I'd never once considered.

lines.japanese: こちらから鳳翔に接触を図るにはどうすればいい？　当然だが、俺はやつの住所も電話番号もメールアドレスも何ひとつ知らない。
lines.english: How was I supposed to contact Kakeru Otori? Naturally, I didn’t know his address, his phone number, or his email. Nothing.

lines.japanese: 連中の溜まり場、ヘテロなんたら……か？
lines.english: Their hangout. Hetero-whatever... maybe?

lines.japanese: 俺は前のめりになっていた体を後ろへ倒し、ソファーの背もたれに体重を預けた。目を閉じると、やつの妹の声が左の壁からかすかに漏れてくる。
lines.english: I let my forward-leaning body fall back against the sofa. When I closed my eyes, his little sister's voice seeped faintly through the wall on my left.

lines.japanese: 何を話しているかまでは判然としないが、同級生と他愛のない言い合いでもしてるみたいだ。
lines.english: I couldn't make out the words, but she seemed to be having some pointless little argument with her classmate.

lines.japanese: ふと、子持ちママチャリ団地妻というフレーズが聞こえた。亜衣の声だ。アノヤロウ、まだ言ってんのか。
lines.english: Then I caught the phrase “apartment wife on a mom-bike with a child seat.” Ai’s voice. That asshole was still on about that?

lines.japanese: ん、そういえば──
lines.english: Hm. Come to think of it—

lines.japanese: ──きのう鳴が言ってた「Ｒ－ウィングは鳴チャリを探している」云々の話題がなかったぞ。
lines.english: —there hadn’t been anything about what Naru told me yesterday: R-Wing searching for the Naru-bike.

lines.japanese: なんでだ？　もっと昔に遡らないと駄目なのか？　いや、それはない。黒パイン咲夜にチャリの件を知られたのは、たしか……そうだ、勤労感謝の日だ。
lines.english: Why? Did I have to go farther back? No, that couldn't be it. Black Pine Sakuya had learned about the bike on... right, Labor Thanksgiving Day.

lines.japanese: 俺はネズミのケツに付いてる団子虫をぐりぐり回して、ふたたび１１月２３日の記事に戻ってみる。
lines.english: I spun the pill bug on the mouse's ass round and round, returning to the posts from November 23.

lines.japanese: 一度はスルーした「特設ページへ」の一文。これが何か関係あるのか？
lines.english: The line I'd skipped before: ‘To the Special Page.’ Did this have something to do with it?

lines.japanese: カーソルとやらをその文字の上へ運んでみると、白い矢印がなぜか人差し指に変わった。思わずネズミの左ボタンを押してみる。
lines.english: When I moved the so-called cursor over the words, the white arrow somehow turned into a pointing finger. Without thinking, I pressed the mouse's left button.

lines.japanese: 一瞬のちに画面が切りかわった。おお、すげえ俺。インターネットの達人だ。
lines.english: A moment later, the screen changed. Whoa. Look at me. Master of the internet.

lines.japanese: 新しい掲示板もほとんど似たような構成だった。しかしよく見ると、いちばん上に「赤い自転車（背もたれ付き）特別捜索本部」とでっかい文字が貼りついていた。
lines.english: The new board had almost the same layout. But at the very top, in enormous letters, was: ‘SPECIAL INVESTIGATION HEADQUARTERS: RED BICYCLE (WITH BACKREST).’

lines.japanese: 赤い自転車……特別捜査本部……。
lines.english: Red bicycle... Special Investigation Headquarters...

lines.japanese: ……なるほど、たしかにコーヒーの一杯も吹きたくなる展開だ。俺は左の壁を同情の視線で眺めた。
lines.english: ...Yes, that was enough to make anybody spray a mouthful of coffee. I looked sympathetically at the wall on my left.

lines.japanese: ブラザー咲夜が発起人となっているその掲示板では、背もたれ付きの赤い自転車に関して、さまざまな情報が寄せられていた。
lines.english: On the board founded by Brother Sakuya, people had submitted all manner of information about red bicycles with backrests.

lines.japanese: まずは該当する条件の市販車が画像付きで紹介され、さらにそのスペックや販売店、買いもとめるオーナーの傾向なんか等どうでもよさげなデータから、柳木原周辺での目撃談まで、多岐に渡った情報が満載だ。
lines.english: First came pictures of commercially available models that fit the description. Then specifications, retailers, the sort of people who bought them, and other seemingly useless data, all the way down to reported sightings around Yanagihara. The place was packed with information.

lines.japanese: 書き込みによれば、やつらは該当車両の情報を皆が携帯し、方々で聞き込み調査まで行っているらしい。
lines.english: According to the posts, everybody carried the target vehicle's particulars and had even gone around questioning people.

lines.japanese: ……無駄に本格的だな。
lines.english: ...Needlessly professional.

lines.japanese: つか、楽しんでるだろ、こいつら。ほとんどオリエンテーリング気分じゃねえか。
lines.english: Hell, they were enjoying this, weren't they? It was practically orienteering.

lines.japanese: ま、うさんくさいけど情報だけはもらっとくかな。
lines.english: Well, dubious or not, I might as well take the information.

lines.japanese: 俺はテレビの横にあったメモ用紙とボールペンを取り、赤い自転車（背もたれ付き）目撃情報のうち、柳木原駅から徒歩圏内の場所に絞ったものを書きうつしていった。
lines.english: I picked up the notepad and ballpoint pen beside the TV and copied out the sightings of red bicycles with backrests within walking distance of Yanagihara Station.

lines.japanese: おし、じゃあ、あしたちょっとこの辺を回ってみるか。闇雲に歩きまわるよりはマシ……かもしれない。
lines.english: Good. Tomorrow I'd make a quick circuit of these places. It might beat wandering around blind... maybe.

lines.japanese: ペンを戻し、メモをポケットにねじ込んだ。またソファーにもたれて息をつく。
lines.english: I put the pen back, stuffed the note into my pocket, and leaned against the sofa with a sigh.

lines.japanese: インターネットっつーのは疲れるんだな。目とか首とか頭とか。もう懲りた。
lines.english: So this internet business was exhausting. Eyes, neck, head. I’d had enough.

lines.japanese: 両手両足を思うさま伸ばして、気が済むと立ちあがった。喉が渇いた。なにか飲んでこよう。
lines.english: I stretched all four limbs as far as they would go, then stood once I was satisfied. I was thirsty. Time to find a drink.

lines.japanese: 俺は空になったグラスを持って個室を出ると、ドリンクコーナーへ向かった。ぬるいジンジャーエールを半分ほど注ぎ、その場で立ったまま飲みほした。
lines.english: I carried my empty glass out of the booth and headed for the drink station. I filled it halfway with lukewarm ginger ale and drained it standing there.

lines.japanese: さて、ガキ共の終電もそろそろだろうし、今日はこの辺で切りあげておこう。
lines.english: The brats' last trains would be along soon. Better call it a night.

lines.japanese: 俺はグラスを返却口に置きすて、さっきまで画面とにらめっこしていたあの部屋──ではなく、その左隣りの部屋へ向かった。
lines.english: I abandoned the glass at the return counter and headed for the room where I'd been glaring at the screen—or rather, the room immediately to its left.

lines.japanese: 薄い仕切り壁の向こうから、鳴と亜衣の黄色い声が聞こえる。俺は簡易扉の取っ手を掴んだ。
lines.english: Naru and Ai's high-pitched voices carried through the thin partition. I took hold of the flimsy door handle.

lines.japanese: 「おー、待たせたな。こっちは終わっ──」
lines.english: “Hey, sorry to keep you waiting. I'm done over—”
“—Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ほわああっ！？」
lines.english: “Whaaa!?”

lines.japanese: 窮屈な密室の中、ふたりの女が場違いな格好をしていた。
lines.english: Within the cramped little room, the two women wore clothes that did not belong there.
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 俺はその異様な光景に、扉を閉めることも忘れて眉間に皺を寄せた。
lines.english: Confronted by the bizarre sight, I forgot even to close the door and furrowed my brow.

lines.japanese: 「ひぁーっ！　けだものー！　今日はだめーっ！」
lines.english: “Eek! You beast! Not today!”

lines.japanese: ……人聞きの悪い悲鳴をあげるガキだ。
lines.english: …What an incriminating scream from the brat.

lines.japanese: まあ、ガキのくせにいっちょまえの体はしてるみたいだけど。少なくとも同い年のもうひとりに比べれば。
lines.english: Still, for a kid, she seemed to have a surprisingly developed body. At least compared with the other girl her age.

lines.japanese: 「え……何やってんのおまえら」
lines.english: “Wait… what are you two doing?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あはは、ちょっと着替えを……」
lines.english: “Ah, ahaha. We were changing…”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それは見りゃ分かるけど、なんでこんなとこで着替える必要があんの」
lines.english: “I can see that. Why do you need to change clothes in a place like this?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、ちょっと服を交換してもらおうと思って。ある筋から隼人君が制服フェチだって聞いたから」
lines.english: “Well, I thought we might swap outfits. I heard through certain channels that you have a thing for school uniforms.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それある筋っつうかナル筋だろ。つーかそれガセだから」
lines.english: “Those ‘certain channels’ were Naru, weren't they? And it's bullshit.”

lines.japanese: 「やぁー、もぉー、とりあえず外に出てくださいよーけだものー！」
lines.english: “Honestly, just go outside for now, you beast!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、そうか悪り──」
lines.english: “Ah, right. Sorry—”

lines.japanese: と、通路に出ようとしたとき、仏頂面をした男の店員がのしのし近付いてくるのが目に入った。
lines.english: I was about to step into the corridor when I saw a male clerk with a sour face lumbering toward us.
“—Oh, shit.”

lines.japanese: 俺は慌てて個室の中に飛びこみ、後ろ手に扉を閉めた。
lines.english: I hurriedly leaped back into the booth and shut the door behind me.

lines.japanese: 「ええー！　ななな、なんで中に入ってくるんですかーけだものー！」
lines.english: “What!? Wh-wh-why are you coming inside, you beast?”

lines.japanese: 「ほんとー、隼人君やらしー、えろえろー」
lines.english: “Honestly, Hayato. So dirty. Such a pervert.”

lines.japanese: 「ばっか、いや、違うんだって。しょーがねえだろ、だっていま、そこに店員がいたんだよ」
lines.english: “Idiots, no, that ain't it. I can't help it. The clerk was right there.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？　店員がいたら外に出らんないの？」
lines.english: “Why? You can’t go outside if there’s a clerk?”

lines.japanese: 「んな当たりま……え？　あれ？　んなことねーか」
lines.english: “Of cour… se? Wait. No, I guess that doesn't matter.”

lines.japanese: 亜衣はにっこり笑顔で頷いてから、右手をひと振りした。
lines.english: Ai smiled brightly, nodded, then flicked her right hand once.

lines.japanese: 「出てけ」
lines.english: “Get out.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 俺は扉を閉めた。
lines.english: I closed the door.

lines.japanese: 「けだものー！」
lines.english: “Beast!”

lines.japanese: ……うるせえなあ。
lines.english: ...Shut up.

lines.japanese: 「ああーっ！　やっばあああ、いまパッド抜いてるの忘れてたあああ！」
lines.english: “Aaah! Oh no! I forgot I took the padding out!”

lines.japanese: ……うるせえっつーの。
lines.english: ...I said shut up.
